newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bildt names U.S. diplomat supervisor for Brcko.
newsitem.headline: Bildt names U.S. diplomat supervisor for Brcko.

text.p: The international community's High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt, said on Friday he had appointed Bill Farrand, a senior U.S. diplomat, as supervisor for the hotly disputed Bosnian town of Brcko.

In a statement released in Vienna ahead of an international conference on the volatile town, claimed by both Serbs and the Moslem-Croat federation, Bildt said: "I warmly welcomed Bill Farrand to the Office of the High Representative as my deputy and supervisor for Brcko."

"He is a vastly experienced foreign service officer and brings all of the right qualities to this very important job," Bildt said. Farrand is a career State Department diplomat with on-the-ground experience in Eastern Europe.
Bildt's announcement came ahead of an international conference on the town's future, attended by all key parties in the Bosnian peace process, in Vienna's historic Hofburg palace.
U.S. arbiter Robert Owen ruled three weeks ago that the Sava river port town should be put under international supervision pending a final decision next year on its status.

Farrand's job will be to strengthen democratic institutions and oversee implementation of the 1995 Dayton peace accord that ended Bosnia's 43-month war. He will be empowered to set up a multi-ethnic police force.
